record.question:
An external audit team uses an established IAM role in its own AWS account. It needs read-only configuration access to selected resources in each of 30 company accounts for a six-week review. The company wants to reuse the auditor’s existing identity and avoid creating local users or long-term access keys.

Which design meets these requirements?

options.text: Provide the auditor with the sign-in credentials of existing company administrators and ask the auditor to perform only read operations.
Create a company directory account for every auditor and build a new federation integration for the review.
Create one IAM user with read-only permissions in the company management account and give its access keys to the auditor as access to all member accounts.

Create an audit role in each target account with scoped read-only permissions and a trust policy for the auditor’s designated role. Authorize the auditor to assume those roles and remove access when the review ends.

explanation.text:
<<4>> places the authorization in the accounts that own the resources. The auditor retains its existing identity and assumes a separate temporary role session for each target account. Scope permissions to the necessary configuration APIs and use identifiable sessions for auditability.

<<1>> shares privileged identities and grants write capabilities even if the auditor promises not to use them. <<2>> can be a valid federation approach, but it duplicates an identity integration and does not meet the requirement to reuse the existing external role. <<3>> introduces long-term keys and assumes that a management-account user automatically gains resource access in member accounts.

Cross-account trust does not grant the caller permission to assume a role by itself; both accounts must authorize the relationship. At the end of an engagement, prevent new sessions and address already issued sessions according to the required revocation timing.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRole.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_third-party.html

diagram_alt: Role ownership stays in each audited account while the auditor reuses one external identity.

sources.supports: Target role trust and source caller permissions are both required for cross-account assumption.
Third-party access through target-account roles avoids sharing persistent credentials.

editorial_notes: Clarified that federation is not inherently insecure; it is unnecessary for this existing-role requirement.
Removed the misconception that a management account identity automatically has member-resource access.
